documents.title: Guidelines on using Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) for Coursework
documents.summary: Official undergraduate coursework policy from the Provost. GenAI is disallowed by default, instructors decide whether to allow it in their courses and are encouraged to say so in the syllabus. Permitted use must be acknowledged, and students who are unsure must ask.
documents.stance_why: The policy says 'Students may not use GenAI tools for submitted coursework unless expressly permitted' and 'GenAI tools are disallowed by default in courses', so AI is banned unless permitted. It also gives instructors authority to allow or disallow, but it sets a default itself and offers no tiers or templates, so restrict rather than delegates.

units.why: The opening line sets the college's framing: GenAI as 'powerful tools for learning'. It is a principle for the whole policy, so P56 (institution-wide framework) with modality informs; it does not itself permit or forbid anything.
units.anchor: Dartmouth recognizes emergent Generative Artificial Intelligence technologies as powerful tools for learning

units.why: The 'Affected Parties' line sets who the policy covers, a scope statement, so P61 (define scope) with modality informs.
units.anchor: All AB undergraduates and special non-degree seeking students.

units.why: 'instructors have authority to determine whether AI tools may be used in their course' hands the decision to each instructor, which is P04; it describes instructor authority so the modality is may.
units.anchor: instructors have authority to determine whether AI tools may be used in their course

units.why: 'requires appropriate acknowledgment' is a disclosure duty on students for submitted work, so P24; modality must, stance permit-with-disclosure.
units.anchor: student use of GenAI tools in submitted work requires appropriate acknowledgment

units.why: This defines GenAI and so sets what the policy covers: P61, modality informs.

units.anchor: Students may not use GenAI tools for submitted coursework unless expressly permitted.

units.why: 'the general rule that GenAI tools are disallowed by default in courses' sets what applies when an instructor has not said otherwise, so P06 (fallback rule); the stated reason 'to permit instructors full autonomy' is part of the same sentence.
